blocks.content: Igneous rocks are called primary rocks because all other rocks are derived from them directly or indirectly.

rows: Cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava
Recrystallization under heat, pressure, and chemical fluids
Foliated or banded, highly crystalline, compact

items: Fossils are present strictly in sedimentary rocks; igneous rocks are non-fossiliferous and crystalline.
Lithification refers to the process of turning loose sediments into consolidated sedimentary rocks through compaction and cementation.
Granite metastasises into Gneiss, Clay/Shale into Slate, and Limestone transforms into Marble under thermal and dynamic metamorphism.
Foliation or lineation is a structural feature exclusive to metamorphic rocks caused by directed pressure during recrystallisation.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Igneous rocks form directly from the cooling and solidification of magma or lava and are classified as primary rocks.
Sedimentary rocks are formed through the weathering, deposition, compaction, and lithification of pre-existing rock fragments.
Metamorphic rocks undergo recrystallisation and reorganisation of minerals under high Pressure, Volume, and Temperature (PVT changes).
Fossils are preserved almost exclusively in sedimentary rocks and are absent in igneous rocks due to intense thermal conditions during cooling.
The Rock Cycle is a continuous geological process wherein older rocks are transformed into new ones through thermal, mechanical, and chemical action.
